name: Open anterior approach to the clavicle
corridor: Subclavicular incision through platysma and clavipectoral fascia to the anterior or anteroinferior clavicle

positioning.text: Position beach-chair or supine on a radiolucent table with the scapula supported and the shoulder freely mobile for reduction of the lateral fragment.

setup.text: Prep the neck, shoulder, and arm; ensure fluoroscopic visualization of the entire clavicle and use guarded drilling because the plexus and subclavian vessels lie deep to the medial-middle junction.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the sternoclavicular and acromioclavicular joints, palpable clavicle, fracture, and planned plate span.

incision.text: Make an oblique incision approximately 8–10 cm long just inferior to and centered on the fracture, curving as needed for medial fixation.

superficial_interval.text: Divide and tag platysma, identify and preserve supraclavicular nerve branches, then open clavipectoral fascia with minimal flap elevation.

deep_interval.text: Expose the anterior clavicle between pectoralis major anteriorly and trapezius posteriorly, preserving periosteal and muscular attachments on comminuted fragments.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, platysma, supraclavicular sensory branches, clavipectoral fascia and periosteum, then clavicle.

structures_encountered.text: Platysma, supraclavicular nerves, clavipectoral fascia, pectoralis major, trapezius, subclavius and periosteum define the exposure.

structures_at_risk.text: Supraclavicular sensory nerves, subclavian vessels, brachial plexus, pleura, and fragment blood supply are at risk.

danger_zones.text: At the medial-middle junction, keep sharp instruments and drill tips controlled against the far cortex; do not sweep blindly beneath the clavicle.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid fixed deep retractors beneath the clavicle and excessive traction on preserved supraclavicular branches or devascularized comminution.

exposure.text: Provides broad visualization of shaft morphology and permits either anterior or superior plate placement through the same general exposure.

limitations.text: Open exposure increases scar and sensory disturbance and risks fragment devascularization if comminution is stripped; plating surface has no universal outcome advantage.

extensions.text: Extend medially or laterally along the clavicle for fixation while preserving ligament and muscle attachments not required for reduction.

indications.text: Applicable to most clavicular shaft fractures selected for open fixation and to selected medial patterns requiring direct reduction.

relative_contraindications.text: Favor a limited or alternative method when indirect reduction is acceptable, the soft-tissue envelope is compromised, or full open visualization would unnecessarily strip comminution.

implant_implications.text: Contour an anterior or anteroinferior plate to the S-shaped clavicle, obtain balanced fixation on both main fragments, and use guarded drilling and measured bicortical screws.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm length, alignment, rotation, plate position, screw length, and avoidance of sternoclavicular and acromioclavicular joints.

closure.text: Cover the plate with a secure clavipectoral fascial-periosteal repair, precisely reapproximate platysma, and close skin without tension.

complications.text: Complications include supraclavicular numbness or neuroma, vascular or plexus injury, pneumothorax, infection, nonunion, hardware irritation or failure, and reoperation.

bailouts.text: If safe far-cortex control or reduction cannot be achieved, enlarge exposure under direct vision or change plate position rather than drilling or clamping blindly.

procedure_applications.condition: A shaft or selected medial fracture requires open reduction with anterior or anteroinferior plate application

questions.question: Which deep structures are most vulnerable near the medial-middle clavicle?
questions.answer: The subclavian artery and vein, brachial plexus, and pleura.

questions.question: Which sensory nerves should be preserved?
Why preserve soft-tissue attachments to comminution?
questions.answer: To maintain fragment perfusion and support union.
